subject: maths-advanced
scope: Planning only, 25 October 2026: exactly the 59 Year 12 Maths Advanced inventory lessons plus the single Year 11 derivative bridge. Actual source explanation and case text was read and all 60 current source bytes match the inventory hashes. This is a visual-purpose plan, not a complete maths, curriculum, advice or selected-script approval. Other Maths courses, other Year 11 lessons and GCSE are outside scope. All codedVisualIds describe planned capabilities unless explicitly identified as existing: the current maths kit has CoordinateAxes, a fixed-window SquareGraph and AlignedAlgebra, not general graphs, secants, distributions, cash-flow models or all assets proposed here. Raster context cannot certify mathematical geometry, values, scale, probability or a financial product. Code all quantities, labels, formulas, axes and answers. Existing raster candidates are visually inspected only where recorded; reuse still needs exact scene-size and teaching review. Built-in imagegen is the proposed later tool, with no generation, media modification or production approval in this plan. Four context/reuse rows and 56 coded-only rows follow actual case needs, without an illustration quota.

families.title: An open box made from a square card
families.purpose: Briefly identify the physical result of cutting equal corner squares and folding a sheet. The raster supplies material and open-top context only; the coded net/fold and dimensions teach why the side length loses two corner widths. It is optional and can be omitted if the coded model already establishes the object clearly.
families.treatment: Restrained painted editorial cutout with a clear open top and simple material texture, subordinate to the exact coded net. Independent object view rather than a measured geometry diagram.

states.description: One independently framed assembled open box. All cut/fold stages remain code, not extra generated variants.
states.prompt: Educational object cutout: a single empty open-top box made by folding an unprinted square of light brown card after equal square corner cutouts. Show a slightly elevated three-quarter view so the square base, four upright side panels and open interior are recognisable; thin card walls with clean straight folds, no lid, no separate flaps, no tabs, no tape, no contents. Use a restrained painted editorial treatment with fine dark outlines and quiet paper texture. Isolate the complete object on true transparent alpha, no room, hand, tools, ground or baked shadow. Natural landscape approximately 4:3 framing with at least 10 percent clear margin around the complete silhouette. No words, numbers, dimensions, rulers, formulas, axes, corner markings or answer hints. This is an uncalibrated context object, not an exact net or scale drawing. The square base and four folded sides must be physically coherent, but no image feature may be used as proof of a length, right angle, optimum or volume. Leave clear exterior space for separate coded annotations if selected.

families.alignment: Single independent context base. No raster-to-net aligned crossfade is claimed. Use a deliberate change of view when switching to the coded overhead net. Reuse this same base unchanged if only x, dimensions or computed volume change; do not scale it as evidence of those changes.

acceptanceChecks: Open top, four continuous sides and square-base construction must be recognisable; reject a lidded carton, extra flap or impossible overlapping panels.
Compare the selected coded net and fold topology with the intended box before any transition is approved. The generated perspective is never measurement evidence.
Confirm no baked labels, dimensions, corner squares or formulas; exact lengths and volume units come from code.
Inspect native dimensions, transparent edges and the complete silhouette at intended desktop and phone scene sizes. Keep the texture quiet enough for the net to remain dominant.
If the object adds no useful identification beyond the coded fold, omit it rather than fill a visual slot.
dependencies: Select the global-extrema open-box scene before generation or reuse integration.
Implement and independently check the exact net, fold and domain in the explainer. Current SquareGraph and algebra do not implement this model.
Student learning review must confirm that the change from physical context to exact net helps the two-width deduction rather than suggesting the illustration proves the optimum.
referenceNeeds: The source specifies a square card with equal corner squares and an open top; no branded packaging reference is needed.
If a selected construction introduces tabs, material thickness or a different assembly, obtain that exact physical reference and revise the model before prompting.

families.title: Delivery van as an unchanged depreciating asset
families.purpose: Identify the asset in the source flat-rate versus reducing-balance comparison and keep physical condition separate from modelled book value. This one vehicle may stay unchanged while code varies valuation, avoiding a false claim that percentage depreciation is visible wear.
families.treatment: Painted editorial cutout consistent with the existing car illustrations, generic and unbranded. No ageing sequence.

states.description: Single ordinary delivery van, retained unchanged throughout any value comparison.
states.prompt: Educational asset-context cutout: one generic compact panel delivery van, intact and in ordinary clean condition, facing right in an almost side-on view with only enough perspective to make the front shape clear. Show a cargo body with solid unmarked side panels, front cab, two visible wheels and coherent wheelbase; no cargo, open doors, delivery worker, logo, company lettering, registration text or recognisable manufacturer badge. Restrained painted editorial treatment, fine dark outlines and subtle paper texture, neutral light-grey body. True transparent alpha background, complete silhouette, no street, ground or baked shadow; landscape approximately 2:1 composition with at least 10 percent clear margin on every side. No currency, numbers, price tag, chart, scale, arrows or formula. The van must not be damaged, rusted, shrinking or fading to encode depreciation. It is an uncalibrated context object only; values and elapsed years will be added as exact coded overlays.

families.alignment: One unchanged base only. Flat-rate and reducing-balance schedules use the identical van image if both are shown. Do not generate worn or smaller value states, crossfade to a different van, or infer a value ratio from raster size.

acceptanceChecks: A panel delivery van must be recognisable; do not substitute a hatchback or imply that inspected Biology car art meets the van case.
Vehicle condition, framing and physical size stay constant while coded values change. No raster detail is evidence of resale price, depreciation rate or mechanical life.
